what_happened.line: The town manager reported that free cash was certified slightly below the estimate, and that retained earnings were certified for the water, sewer and trash enterprise funds.
The committee went through suggested edits to the investment policy; it is to be cleaned up and brought back, with action planned for November 8.
The library director asked for money to pay staff for fifth-grade visits, which take staff hours with no money budgeted; it would likely fold into article one.
The updated DPW union contract figure is lower than first stated because of retirements and attrition, and is funded from the salary reserve.
The Personnel Committee plans to table the salary survey article (article eight) at town meeting.

why_it_matters: Free cash and the salary reserve are the town budget's one-time and reserve money, mostly from taxes, so how they are certified and spent at town meeting affects what is left for later needs and the tax rate.
The investment policy governs how town funds are held and invested, and the committee's recommended version is due for action on November 8.
watch_next: November 8: the committee meets to cover warrant articles, town meeting voting procedures and action on the investment policy.
The special town meeting, where the library staff-hours request, the DPW contract article and the salary survey article (article eight) are to come up.
